title: Site changes: a brief's writes read Type Tracy setup (one row per run), a seat key's writes read API, a /v1 revert is its own row — from provenance the Apply door recorded, never from a missing session
steps: S1: Call the Apply door as a person with a setup run (applyAs … { setupRun }), then without one; read site_write.origin/origin_ref.
S2: Call it with a seat key principal, and over HTTP as a chat whose x-tracy-session looks like a key's (key:<16>); read origin.
S3: Call apply.revert with a key; read the row's target.
S4: Classify writes in JS (classifyWrites) and through the V2 SQL CASE on the same rows: setup run writes, a session-less write with no record, key writes with and without origin api, a key's revert.
expect: S1: origin 'setup', origin_ref the run, actor the person; the call without a run has origin null.
S2: the key's write has origin 'api' and origin_ref the key id; the chat's has origin null.

S4: JS and SQL agree: setup:<run> is ONE row of source setup; the session-less write with no record stays unknown; session:key:<id> with origin api is api, without it unknown; the revert is its own write:<id> row of source api.
evidence: tasks/evidence/e2e-full-dev/2026-10-04/TRIAGE-2026-10-11.md rows 2 and 4 (g65-* brief runs: 7/49/154 Unknown rows)
fence: Apply door records origin from the principal and applyAs only; activity-source classifies only on that record

tests: sweep 4: a write made for a person from their brief is recorded as Tracy setup, under its run
sweep 2: a seat key’s write is recorded as the key’s; a chat header shaped like a key’s is not
sweep 2: a revert names the change it takes back
sweep 4: Tracy setup only from the provenance the door recorded
sweep 2: an API key write is API only when the door recorded it as the key’s
every other table: turns, writes, outside rows and operations classify the same in SQL and JS
